name: RTS — Ban / Timeout Widget
description: Turn moderation into an event with a cinematic ban animation, independent timeout cells, configurable positioning, sizing, messages, and a proper event queue.

setup.title: Get the extension running.
setup.intro: Import the Streamer.bot actions, enable them, add the overlay to OBS, then test the extension.

steps.title: Import the extension into streamer.bot
steps.description: Open Streamer.bot and use Import to paste the supplied import string, or download the latest import file and import it into Streamer.bot.

substeps.title: Copy the import string
substeps.text: Look above for Action Import, click the [Copy Import ⧉] Button, then paste the import code into Streamer.Bot's Import dialog.

images.alt: The RTS extension import code with an arrow pointing to the import code button

substeps.title: Open Import
substeps.text: Select Import from the Streamer.bot toolbar.

images.alt: Streamer.bot import screen showing the RTS extension import code

substeps.title: Paste the import code
substeps.text: Paste the supplied import string into the Import String box, then select Import.

substeps.title: Confirm the import
substeps.text: Review the actions being imported, then select Import to continue.

steps.title: Enable the imported actions
steps.description: Enable the imported RTS actions so the extension can respond to events.

substeps.title: Enable the extension actions
substeps.text: Enable the imported RTS actions in Streamer.bot.

images.alt: Streamer.bot imported RTS actions being enabled

substeps.title: Check and Enable the commands
substeps.text: Confirm the imported extension commands are present and enabled where required.

images.alt: Streamer.bot commands showing the imported RTS extension commands

steps.title: Add the extension overlay to OBS
steps.description: Add the extension's hosted overlay URL as an OBS Browser Source, or use the supplied local overlay files.

substeps.title: Copy the Overlay Url
substeps.text: Look above in the Quick Access section and click the [Copy Overlay URL ⧉] Button, This will copy the overlay URL to your clipboard for use in OBS.

images.alt: RTS copy overlay URL button screenshot

substeps.title: Create a browser source
substeps.text: Add a browser source to an existing or newly created scene in OBS.

images.alt: OBS add a new browser source dialog

substeps.title: Configure the browser source
substeps.text: Paste the Overlay Url you just copied into the URL field, then set the width and height to 1920x1080 or your screen size if its diffirent make sure you dimensions that are 16:9 or the overlay will be distorted, and check Refresh browser when scene becomes active.

steps.title: Configure Settings and Test the extension
steps.description: In the Actions Panel look for Extensions Settings Action

substeps.title: Open the settings dialog
substeps.text: In the Actions Panel look for Extensions Settings Action and click to select it, Right click the the trigger called 'Core Test' and click Test Trigger top open the dialog

substeps.title: Automatic Installation of the RtsUI.dll
substeps.text: If you do not have the dll installed, the extension will download and place it your streamer.bot installation directory.

substeps.title: Automatic Updating of the RtsUI.dll
substeps.text: If the extension requires an updated version, it will ask you if you want it to download and install the latest version.
